pool.text: Conquistador Pedro de Valdivia founded Santiago del Nuevo Extremo on February 12.
A devastating earthquake struck Santiago, resulting in the death of over 600 people.
The First Government Junta was proclaimed in Santiago, marking independence beginnings.
The Spanish army progress was halted at the Battle of Maipú.
The first telegraph system connecting the capital to Valparaíso was inaugurated.
The Municipal Theater of Santiago was built by the French architect Brunet.
Los Cerrillos Airport opened alongside the expansion of the telephone network.
The National Stadium emerged following shifts in popular entertainment venues.
The Intercommunal Plan of Santiago was released proposing an urban limit.
The Santiago Metropolitan Park was established on Cerro San Cristóbal.
The new Pudahuel International Airport was opened for travelers.
The Torre Entel television tower with observation deck was completed.
The first phase of the Santiago Metro was opened.
A fire in the Torre Santa María killed 11 people.
Santiago officially became part of the Union of Ibero-American Capital Cities.
A powerful earthquake struck the city causing minimal casualties and destroying buildings.
The Congress was newly constituted in Valparaíso after the military dictatorship.
The International Theater Festival known as Santiago a Mil takes place every January.
The Library of Santiago at Barrio Matucana was opened to the public.
The master plan known as Transantiago was established.
